An additional $3.5 million was raised from advertising revenue, and was donated to other charities.[94] The day before the special aired, fellow free agents Chris Bosh and Dwyane Wade announced they would sign with Miami.[95][96] James joined with Bosh and Wade in part so he could shoulder less of the offensive load, and he thought he would have a better chance of winning an NBA championship with the Heat.[97] Heat president Pat Riley played a major role in convincing James to play on the team with Bosh and Wade.[98] James would be relieved of the burden of scoring, and thought he could be the first player since Oscar Robertson to average a triple-double in a season.[97] James, Bosh and Wade were referred to as an NBA superteam.[99]

Upon leaving the Cavaliers, James drew criticism from executives, fans, and current and former players.[100] The Decision was viewed as unnecessary. Many thought the prolonged wait for James' choice was unprofessional, as not even the teams courting him were aware of his decision until moments before the show.[101] Upon learning that James would not be returning to Cleveland, Cavaliers owner Dan Gilbert published a letter to fans in which he denounced James' actions.[102] Some angry fans of the team recorded videos of themselves burning his jersey.[103] Former NBA players, including Michael Jordan and Magic Johnson, were critical of James, condemning him for forming a superteam with Bosh and Wade in Miami and not trying to win a championship in Cleveland.[104][105][106] Some commentators defended James' decision to join Miami by noting the Cavaliers' inability to build strong support around him. They argued other NBA greats had benefitted from talented teammates.[107] James drew further criticism in an interview with CNN when he claimed race might have been a factor in the fallout from The Decision.[108][109] The phrase "taking my talents to South Beach" became a punch line for critics.[110][111] James later expressed regret over his handling of The Decision.[f]

James signed a 6-year, $110 million contract with the Heat on July 10, 2010.[g] He changed his jersey number to 6, as the number 23 was retired in Miami for Michael Jordan.[119][120] The Heat threw a welcome party for the "Big Three" at the American Airlines Arena, during which James declared that the Heat would win multiple championships.[h] Outside Miami, the spectacle was badly received, furthering negative perception of James.[124]

Throughout the 2010–11 season, the media and opposing fans treated James as a villain.[125] The Heat struggled to adjust to these new circumstances, going only 9–8 after 17 games.[126] James later admitted the negativity made him play with an angrier demeanor.[125] On December 2, James faced the Cavaliers in Cleveland for the first time since departing.[127] He scored 38 points and led Miami to victory while being booed every time he touched the ball.[128] The Heat turned their season around and finished as the East's second seed.[129]

In the Eastern Conference Semifinals, the Heat was matched with the Boston Celtics.[130] In Game 5, James scored Miami's last 10 points to seal a series-clinching win.[131] After the buzzer, James knelt in an emotional moment, later telling reporters it was an extremely personal victory for him and the team.[132] The Heat advanced to the Finals, where they lost to the Dallas Mavericks.[133] James' Finals average of 17.8 points per game was a 9-point drop from the regular season, the largest drop-off in league history.[134][135]

The 2011–12 season was delayed by a lockout. During that summer, James worked with Hakeem Olajuwon to improve his post up game.[i] As the start of the season approached, James set a goal for himself to leave behind the "villain role" that he had embraced, and said he was hoping to regain a sense of joy on the court.[125] Miami began the year with a franchise-best 18–6 record, and James was named MVP for the third time.[j]

In the second round of the playoffs, Miami lost Bosh to an abdominal injury and found themselves trailing the Indiana Pacers two games to one.[141] James responded with a 40-point, 18-rebound, and nine-assist outing in Game 4 to even the series.[142] To compensate for Bosh's absence, the Heat embraced a small-ball lineup with James at power forward, which they retained after Bosh's return in the conference finals against the Boston Celtics.[143][144] Facing elimination in Game 6, James recorded 45 points and 15 rebounds to lead the Heat to victory in a "career-defining performance".[145] Miami won Game 7 to advance to the Finals, earning them a matchup with the Oklahoma City Thunder and James' rival Kevin Durant.[146][147] In Game 5, James registered a triple-double as Miami defeated Oklahoma for their second-ever championship and James' first.[148] James was voted the NBA Finals Most Valuable Player (MVP) with averages of 28.6 points, 10.2 rebounds, and 7.4 assists.[149] His full postseason run, in which he averaged 30.3 points, 9.7 rebounds, and 5.6 assists, was ranked the second best in modern NBA history.[150]

In February of the 2012–13 season, James averaged 29.7 points and 7.8 assists while setting shooting efficiency records.[151][152] The Heat began a 27-game winning streak, which is the third longest in NBA history.[153] James' performance was described as a "month for the ages".[154] Miami finished with a franchise and league best 66–16 record,[155] and James was named MVP for the fourth time, falling one vote shy of becoming the first player to win unanimously.[156]

In Game 1 of the Eastern Conference Finals, James scored a buzzer-beating layup to give Miami a one-point victory against the Pacers.[157] The Heat won the series and advanced to the Finals,[158] where they faced the San Antonio Spurs, a rematch for James from his first Finals six years earlier.[159] James was criticized for his lack of aggressiveness and poor shot selection, as Miami fell behind 2–3.[82][160][161] In Game 6, James recorded his second triple-double of the series, including 16 fourth quarter points, to lead the Heat to a comeback victory.[162] In Game 7, he tied the Finals record for most points scored in a Game 7 victory, with 37 points.[163] James was named Finals MVP for the second straight season, averaging 25.3 points, 10.9 rebounds, 7.0 assists, and 2.3 steals for the championship round.[164]

On March 3 of the 2013–14 season, James scored a career-high, and franchise-record, 61 points against the Charlotte Bobcats.[165] He converted his first eight three-point field goal attempts through three quarters, setting a record for the most three-point field goals made in a 60-point game. James set the record for most points in a single game while wearing a mask.[166] In the second round of the playoffs, James tied a career postseason-high by scoring 49 points in Game 4 against the Brooklyn Nets.[167] In the next round, Miami defeated the Pacers to earn their fourth consecutive Finals berth, becoming one of only four teams to do so.[168] In Game 1 of the NBA Finals, James missed most of the fourth quarter because of leg cramps, helping San Antonio take an early series lead.[169] In Game 2, he led the Heat to a series-tying victory with 35 points on a 64 percent shooting rate.[170] San Antonio eliminated the Heat in five games, ending Miami's quest for a three-peat.[171] For the Finals, James averaged 28.2 points, 7.8 rebounds, and 2.0 steals.[172]

In June 2014, James opted out of his contract with the Heat, and on July 1, became an unrestricted free agent.[173] On July 11, James revealed via a first-person essay in Sports Illustrated that he intended to return to the Cavaliers.[174] In contrast to The Decision, his announcement to return was well received.[175][176][177] The next day, James signed a two-year, $42 million contract,[178] marking his return to the team who had compiled a league-worst 97–215 record in the four seasons following his departure.[179] The Cavaliers acquired Kevin Love, forming a star trio along with Kyrie Irving.[180] James switched back to No. 23 upon his return.[181]

In January of the 2014–2015 season, James missed two weeks due to left knee and lower back strains; at the time the longest stretch of missed games in his career.[184] In the second round of the playoffs, he hit a baseline jumper at the buzzer to give Cleveland a 2–2 series tie with the Chicago Bulls.[185] In the Eastern Conference Finals, the Cavaliers defeated the Atlanta Hawks to advance to the NBA Finals, making James the first player since the 1960s to play in five consecutive Finals.[186] For most of the Finals against the Golden State Warriors, Irving and Love were sidelined due to injury, giving James more offensive responsibilities.[186] Behind his leadership, the Cavaliers took a 2–1 series lead,[187] but lost in six games.[188] Despite this, he received serious consideration for the Finals MVP Award,[189] averaging 35.8 points, 13.3 rebounds, and 8.8 assists.[190]

In the 2015 offseason, James declined his $21.5 million player option and re-signed on a two-year, $47 million contract that carried a second year player option.[191] During the 2015–16 season, James was criticized for off-court controversies, including the firing of Cavaliers' coach David Blatt.[192][193] Despite these distractions, Cleveland finished with 57 wins and the best record in the East.[194] In the playoffs, the Cavaliers advanced to the NBA Finals, losing only two games en route to a rematch with the Golden State Warriors,[194] who were coming off a record-setting 73-win season.[195]

To begin the series, Cleveland fell behind 3–1.[196] James responded by registering 41-point games in Games 5 and 6, leading the Cavaliers to consecutive wins to stave off elimination.[197] In Game 7, he posted a triple-double and made key plays, including a chasedown block on Andre Iguodala's go-ahead layup attempt,[198] as Cleveland emerged victorious, winning the city's first professional sports title in 52 years and becoming the first team to come back from a 3–1 deficit in the Finals.[199] James became the third player to record a triple-double in an NBA Finals Game 7,[200] and, with series averages of 29.7 points, 11.3 rebounds, 8.9 assists, 2.3 blocks, and 2.6 steals per game,[196] became the first in league history to lead both teams in all five statistical categories for a playoff round, culminating in unanimous Finals MVP selection.[201]

James again opted out of his contract and re-signed with the Cavaliers, this time on a three-year, $100 million contract, in which the final year was a player option.[202] The 2016–17 season was marred by injuries and unexpected losses for the Cavaliers;[203] James described it as one of the "strangest" years of his career.[204] Following a January defeat to the New Orleans Pelicans, James criticized Cleveland's front office for constructing a team he felt was too "top heavy", for which he received countercriticism.[205] The Cavaliers finished the season as the East's second seed, with James averaging 26.4 points and career highs in rebounds (8.6), assists (8.7), and turnovers (4.1) per game.[83]

In Game 3 of the first round of the playoffs, he registered 41 points, 13 rebounds, and 12 assists against the Indiana Pacers, leading Cleveland to a comeback victory after trailing by 25 points at halftime, representing the largest halftime deficit overcome in NBA playoff history.[206] In Game 5 of the Eastern Conference Finals against the Boston Celtics, James scored 35 points and surpassed Jordan as the league's all-time postseason scoring leader. The Cavaliers advanced to the NBA Finals for the third consecutive year, a rematch with the Warriors.[207] In Game 4, James logged a triple-double of 31 points, 10 rebounds, and 11 assists, as Cleveland staved off elimination with a 137–116 win after trailing 3–0. His ninth Finals triple-double, he passed Magic Johnson for the most triple-doubles in NBA Finals history.[208] The Cavaliers lost in five games, despite James's double-double of 41 points, 13 rebounds and eight assists in game 5.[209] Averaging 33.6 points, 12.0 rebounds, and 10.0 assists, James became the first player to average a triple-double in the Finals.[210]

Before the 2017–18 season, the Cavaliers overhauled their roster by trading Irving to the Boston Celtics, who requested a trade in part because he no longer wanted to play with James.[211] After a slow start, Cleveland rebounded by winning 18 of 19 games.[212] Their turnaround began with a victory over the Wizards on November 3 where James scored 57 points, the second-highest point total of his career and a franchise record.[213] In January, the Cavaliers had a losing record, and James was criticized for his lackluster effort.[214] The next month, James won his third All-Star Game MVP Award, after posting 29 points, 10 rebounds, eight assists, and key plays to help Team LeBron beat Team Curry.[215] Following trades in February, Cleveland returned to form and James reached several historical milestones; on March 30, he set an NBA record with 867 straight games scoring in double digits.[216] James finished the season with averages of 27.5 points, 8.6 rebounds, 9.2 assists, and 4.2 turnovers per game.[83] On April 11, James played all 82 games for the first time in his career.[217]

In the first two rounds of the the playoffs, James made two-game winning buzzer beaters against the Pacers and the Raptors, respectively.[218] In the Eastern Conference finals, the Cavaliers defeated the Celtics, giving James his eighth consecutive NBA Finals appearance and sending Cleveland to their fourth straight Finals against Golden State Warriors.[219] In Game 1, James scored a playoff career-high 51 points in a 124–114 overtime loss.[220] Afterwards, James injured his hand punching a locker room wall, which hampered him for the remainder of the series.[221] The Cavaliers lost in the first NBA Finals sweep since 2007.[222]

In June 2018, James opted out of his contract with the Cavaliers and became an unrestricted free agent.[223] He signed with the Los Angeles Lakers on a four-year, $153.5 million contract;[224][225] James' agent Rich Paul explained: "In 2010, when he went to Miami, it was about championships. In 2014, when he went back to Cleveland, it was about delivering on a promise. In 2018, it was just about doing what he wants to do."[226] Reaction was more positive than his original departure from the Cavaliers, albeit mixed, as some onlookers felt LA was not his best destination.[227]

The Lakers expected James to immediately transform them into a championship contender after having missed the playoffs since 2014.[228][229] The team rounded out their roster with a controversial collection of playmakers and veterans. To begin the 2018–19 season, the Lakers struggled to find effective lineups and recorded only two wins through their first seven games.[230] In November, they began a turnaround, which included two of James' strongest performances of the season. On November 14, he registered 44 points, 10 rebounds, and nine assists in a victory against the Portland Trail Blazers.[231] Four days later, James scored a season-high 51 points in a victory over the Heat.[232] After blowing out the Golden State Warriors on Christmas Day, Los Angeles improved their record to 20–14, but James suffered a groin injury,[233] the first major injury of his career.[234] James missed a then career-high 17 consecutive games, and the Lakers fell out of playoff contention,[233] marking the first time James missed the playoffs since 2005.[235] He was later ruled out for the rest of the season.[236] Despite his inconsistent campaign, James was named to the All-NBA Third Team, marking the first time in twelve years he did not make the All-NBA First Team.[237]

During the offseason, the Lakers hired Frank Vogel as their new head coach, and traded most of their young core to the Pelicans for big man Anthony Davis.[238] James embraced the much-improved roster by moving to full-time point guard, and competing with a more consistent defensive effort.[239] Behind James' leadership, the Lakers opened the 2019–20 season with a 17–2 record, matching the best start in franchise history.[240] On January 25, 2020, James passed Kobe Bryant for third on the all-time regular season scoring list, a day before Bryant died in a helicopter crash.[241][242] On January 31, James delivered an improvised eulogy in honor of Bryant, describing him as a "brother" and expressing a desire to continue his legacy.[243][244]

Before the season was suspended due to Covid, James led the Lakers to a victory over the Milwaukee Bucks in a matchup of conference leaders, followed by a streak-breaking victory over the Los Angeles Clippers.[245] James ended the regular season as the league leader in assists for the first time in his career, averaging 10.2 assists per game.[246] He earned a record 16th All-NBA Team selection as part of the First Team, extending his record First Team selections to 13.[247]

The Lakers entered the playoffs as the top seed in the West and advanced to the NBA Finals.[248] In Game 5 of the Western Conference Finals against the Denver Nuggets, James helped clinch the conference championship by scoring 38 points, including 16 in the fourth quarter.[249] In the Finals, James and teammates matched up with his former team, the Miami Heat, and took control of the series with a 2–0 lead.[250] In Game 5, James had his best statistical performance of the Finals with 40 points, 13 rebounds, and seven assists.[251] The Lakers eliminated the Heat in Game 6, earning James his fourth NBA championship. With averages of 29.8 points, 11.8 rebounds, and 8.5 assists per game, James was named the Finals MVP, and became the only player to win the award with three different franchises.[252][253]

James signed a two-year, $85.7 million extension that kept him with the Lakers through the 2022–23 season.[254]
The 2020–21 season, shortened due to Covid, began in December with a 116–109 loss to the Los Angeles Clippers.[255] On December 31, James became the first player in NBA history to score 10 points or more in 1,000 consecutive games in a 121–107 victory over the San Antonio Spurs.[256] On February 18, 2021, James became the third player in NBA history with 35,000 career points, joining Hall of Famers Abdul-Jabbar and Karl Malone.[257] On March 20, James sprained his ankle against the Atlanta Hawks,[258] but was able to hit a three-point shot afterwards to keep his 10-points streak alive before exiting.[259] By March, the Lakers were No. 2, two games behind the Utah Jazz, but went 14–16 without Davis and 6–10 without James, falling to No. 5.[260] James returned on April 30 after missing 20 games, the longest absence of his career.[261]

In May, James was sidelined again after leaving a game against the Toronto Raptors,[262] but he returned for the final two games,[263][264] and finished the season averaging of 25.0 points, his 17th consecutive season averaging at least 25 points per game, the most in NBA history.[265] In an injury-laden season, the Lakers ended with a 42–30 record, finishing No. 7 due to tiebreakers, earning them a spot in play-in tournament.[266] Against the Warriors, the Lakers won 103–100, with James hitting the game-winning three-pointer, and posting a triple-double with 22 points, 11 rebounds, and 10 assists.[267] His 34-foot (10 m) shot over Stephen Curry before the shot clock buzzer was his longest basket of the season, as well as his longest go-ahead shot in the closing three minutes in his career.[268][269]

In the first round of the playoffs, the Lakers faced the No. 2 Phoenix Suns. This marked the first time in James' career he did not have home court advantage in the opening series.[270][271] They were up 2–1 before Davis suffered a strained groin in Game 4, in which James finished with 25 points on 10-for-21 shooting, 12 rebounds, and 6 assists.[272] The Lakers lost to the Suns in six games, marking the first time James lost in the first round.[270] James finished the series averaging 23.3 points, his lowest mark since averaging 22.8 in the 2014 Eastern Conference finals.[273] He made his 17th consecutive All-NBA Team selection,[274] extending the record for most selections,[275] being named for the third time to the All-NBA Second Team.[276]

For the 2021–22 season, James switched his jersey back to No. 6; he had intended to do so two years earlier, to allow Davis to wear No. 23, but Nike prevented him from doing so, due to having too much merchandise of James with No. 23.[277] In a game against the Pistons on November 21, James was ejected in the third quarter after getting into a scuffle with Isaiah Stewart during the 121–116 victory. This was only the second time he was ejected,[278] and James was suspended for one game.[279] In his next 16 games, James averaged 30.4 points, 8.9 rebounds, 6.3 assists, 1.6 steals, and 1.4 blocks on 54 percent shooting, also achieving his 100th triple-double,[280] while becoming the third NBA player to surpass 36,000 career points;[281] James played 35 percent of his minutes at center.[282][283] From December 19 to February 26, 2022, he had a streak of 23 consecutive 25-point games.[284]

In December, James became the second player in NBA history, after Jordan, to post 40 points and no turnovers at age 35 or older.[285] In January, James met the minimum criteria for points per game by playing at least 70 percent of his team's games, averaging 28.6 points, and became the oldest player to average 25+ points per game, having already been the youngest to do so, as James averaged 27.6 points per game in his sophomore season at 20 years old.[286][unreliable NBA source] He became the oldest player at 37, to record at least 25 points in ten straight NBA games.[287] James became the first player to record at least 30,000 career points, 10,000 career rebounds, and 9,000 career assists.[288][289][290] He surpassed Robertson for fourth all-time free throws made,[291][unreliable NBA source] and Alvin Robertson for 10th all-time in career steals.[292][293] In February, James surpassed Abdul-Jabbar for the most points scored in both the regular season and playoffs.[294] James set a record for most turnovers in a career, surpassing Karl Malone's record of 4,524 turnovers.[295] By March, he passed Malone for second in the all-time minutes and regular season scoring lists.[296][297][298] At the 2022 NBA All-Star Game, James was celebrated among the other 74 players for the NBA 75th Anniversary Team.[299] James led all players in fan votes with his 18th All-Star selection, tying Bryant and just one behind Abdul-Jabbar;[300] his team achieved its fifth consecutive All-Star victory,[301] defeating Team Durant 163–161,[302] with James hitting the game-winning dagger shot in front of his hometown crowd.[303][304]

In March, James recorded two 50-point games,[305][306] becoming the oldest player to have multiple 50-point games in a season; it was James' 15th 50-point game.[307] He recorded his 10,000th career assist, becoming the only player in NBA history to record at least 10,000 points, 10,000 rebounds, and 10,000 assists.[308][309] Due to an ankle injury in March, he missed out on a close three-players run for the NBA scoring title,[310][311][312] having only played 56 games, two less than the necessary to qualify;[313] aged 37, James would have broken Jordan's record of oldest scoring leader at 34.[314] Bill Oram wrote that James' injury felt like "the moment that might signal the end of the Lakers season".[315][316] The Lakers were eliminated from playoff and play-in contention for the first time since 2019 (James' first season with the Lakers) after a 121–110 loss to the Phoenix Suns.[317] James was ruled out the rest of the season due to soreness in his left ankle.[318] James was named to the All-NBA Third Team for the second time; it was his 18th consecutive All-NBA Team selection, extending the record for most selections.[319]

In August 2022, James signed a two-year, $97 million contract extension with the Lakers, which had a player option in the second year.[320][321] The contract made him the highest-paid athlete in NBA history at $529 million, surpassing Kevin Durant in all-time earnings.[322] On October 28, James posted 28 points, seven rebounds, five assists, and four steals in an 111–102 loss to the Minnesota Timberwolves. He recorded his 1,135th career 20-point game, passing Karl Malone.[323] On December 13, James scored 33 points in a 122–118 overtime loss to the Celtics, surpassing Wilt Chamberlain for the second-most 30-point games in NBA history, 516, in 1,386 career appearances.[324] On his 38th birthday, James scored 47 points on 18-for-27 shooting from the field, along with 10 rebounds and nine assists in a victory over the Atlanta Hawks.[325]

On January 9, 2023, James received his 66th Player of the Week award, doubling the career total of runner-up Bryant.[326] Four days later, he became the second player in NBA history to reach 38,000 points.[327] On January 16, James had a season high 48 points in a victory over the Houston Rockets. It was his 100th career game with 40 or more points – including the postseason.[328] On January 23, James scored 46 points, including a career-high nine 3-pointers, in a loss to the Clippers, becoming the first player to score at least 40 points in a game, against all NBA franchises.[329][330] On January 19, James was named as a starter at the 2023 NBA All-Star Game, tying Abdul-Jabbar's record for the most All-Star selections (19). It was James' 19th consecutive All-Star appearance, surpassing Bryant's previous mark.[331] On January 31, James put up a triple-double with 28 points, 10 rebounds, and 11 assists in a 129–123 overtime victory over the New York Knicks, becoming the first player in NBA history to put up a triple-double in his 20th season. He surpassed Mark Jackson and Steve Nash for fourth on the all-time career assists list.[332][333]

On February 7, 2023, James passed Abdul-Jabbar as the all-time leading scorer in NBA history.[334] The NBA stopped the game with 10.9 seconds left in the third quarter for an on-court ceremony, where he received the game ball from Abdul-Jabbar.[335] James gave a speech and embraced Abdul-Jabbar.[336][337] James missed the following three games due to ankle soreness.[338][339] On February 19, Team LeBron lost the 2023 NBA All-Star Game 184–175 to Team Giannis, marking the first time James lost an All-Star game as a captain.[k] He had been undefeated (5–0) as a captain, and since the format was changed in 2018.[341] During the game, James suffered a right hand contusion and was ruled out for the 2nd half.[342]

On February 26, James sustained a right foot injury in the Lakers' comeback win against Dallas Mavericks.[343][344] After a 13-game absence, James made his return on March 26 against the Chicago Bulls.[345][346] On April 2, James put up a triple-double with 18 points, 10 rebounds, and 11 assists in a 134–109 victory over the Houston Rockets, tying Jason Kidd for fourth place on the all-time career triple-doubles list.[347] Two days later, James put up 37 points, five rebounds, six assists, a steal, a block, and a game-winning layup in a 135–133 overtime victory over the Utah Jazz.[348] On April 9, in the final game of the 2022–23 season, James posted 36 points, six rebounds, and six assists to lead the Lakers to a 128–117 victory over the Jazz.[349] James finished the regular season with averages of 28.9 points, 8.3 rebounds and 6.8 assists per game, becoming the oldest player in NBA history to average at least 25 points, five rebounds, and five assists in a season.[350] In Game 4 of the first-round series against the Memphis Grizzlies, James had 22 points, a playoff career-high 20 rebounds, and seven assists in a 117–111 overtime victory, marking his first 20–20 game of his career.[351] He became the oldest player in league history with at least 20 points and 20 rebounds in a playoff game.[352] In Game 6 of the Western Conference semifinals, James put up 30 points, nine rebounds, nine assists and two steals, in a 122–101 victory over Golden State Warriors to lead the Lakers to the 2023 Western Conference finals. He also won his 41st playoff series, surpassing Derek Fisher for the most playoff series wins in NBA history.[353][354] In the Western Conference finals, the Lakers were swept by the eventual NBA champion Denver Nuggets; James set his playoff record with 31 points in the first half.[355]

For the 2023–24 season, James switched back to jersey No. 23 from No. 6 in honor of Bill Russell, who had died the previous year and whose No. 6 jersey had been retired league-wide.[356] With the retirements of Udonis Haslem and Andre Iguodala, James became the NBA's oldest active player.[357] On November 1, James put up 35 points in a 130–125 overtime victory over the Los Angeles Clippers. His 35 points were his 81st 30-point game since turning 35, surpassing Karl Malone for the most 30-point games by any player since turning 35 in NBA history.[358] On November 15, James logged 28 points, 10 rebounds and 11 assists in a 125–110 loss to the Sacramento Kings, becoming the second-oldest player to have recorded a triple-double. Four days later, James scored a season-high 37 points in a narrow 105–104 win over the Houston Rockets. He tied Vince Carter for seventh on the all-time three-pointers made list with 2,290.[359] In November, James became the first player in NBA history to reach 5,000 career turnovers.[360]

On November 21, in a 131–99 victory over the Utah Jazz, he became the first player in league history to reach 39,000 career points.[361] Six days later, in a 138–94 loss to the Philadelphia 76ers, James surpassed Abdul-Jabbar to become the player with the most minutes played in NBA games during the regular season and playoffs.[362] The 44-point loss was the worst of James' career.[363] On December 9, James and the Lakers won the inaugural NBA In-Season Tournament, with James receiving the Tournament MVP award and being selected to the All-Tournament team.[364]

On January 25, 2024, James was named an All-Star starter for the 2024 NBA All-Star Game, marking his 20th NBA All-Star selection, surpassing Abdul-Jabbar for the most All-Star selections.[365] Two days later, James put up a triple-double with 36 points, a career-high 20 rebounds, and 12 assists, including a pair of game-winning free throws, in a 145–144 double overtime victory over the Golden State Warriors,[366] becoming the first in Lakers history since Abdul-Jabbar in 1976 to put up at least 30 points, 20 rebounds, and 10 assists in a game.[367] On February 28, James led the Lakers to a 116–112 comeback win against the Los Angeles Clippers. Trailing by 21 points entering the fourth quarter, he outscored the Clippers by himself 19–16 in the final quarter, going 5-for-8 from three-point range. It was the largest fourth-quarter comeback of James' career.[368][369] Three days later, James became the first player in NBA history to reach 40,000 career points.[370] On March 16, he scored a season-high 40 points in a loss to the Warriors.[371] On March 31, James put up 40 points on a career-high nine three-pointers in a 116–104 victory over the Brooklyn Nets. He surpassed Jordan for the most 30-point games, across the regular season and playoffs, with 672.[372][373] On April 2, James passed Oscar Schmidt to become the world's all-time scoring leader in basketball history.[374] In the season finale on April 14 against the Pelicans, James scored 28 points, brought down 11 rebounds, and his 17 assists pushed his career total over the 11k mark.[375]

James finished his 21st season in the NBA averaging 25.7 points, 8.3 assists and 7.3 rebounds a game. He shot 54% from the field and a career-high 41% from 3-point range, making him the first player to average over 25 points and eight assists while shooting at least 50% overall and 40% from beyond the arc for an entire season.[376] On the road against the Pelicans in the play-in game, James had 23 points, nine rebounds, and nine assists to win 110–106 and clinch his 17th career playoff appearance.[377] After the Lakers fell into a 3–0 series deficit in the first round against the Denver Nuggets, James scored 14 of his 30 points in the fourth quarter in Game 4 as the Lakers won 119–108 to stave off elimination.[378] In the process, James recorded his 19th career 30-point game when facing elimination and improved to 15–12 in 27 career elimination games.[379] The Lakers lost the series, despite James' 30-point and 11-rebound double-double in a 108–106 closeout loss in Game 5.[380]

On July 6, 2024, James re-signed with the Lakers on a two-year, $104 million contract which carried a no-trade clause and had a player option in the second year.[381] James' son Bronny had been drafted 55th overall by the Lakers. This marked the first father-son duo in NBA history.[382] On October 22, in a game against the Minnesota Timberwolves, James and Bronny became the first father-son duo to appear in an NBA game together.[383] During his 2024–25 season debut, he tied Carter for the record for the most NBA seasons played.[384] On November 13, he logged a triple-double of 35 points, 12 rebounds, and 14 assists, in a 128–123 victory against the Memphis Grizzlies. Aged 39 years and 319 days, he broke his record set in 2019 for the oldest player to record a triple-double in three consecutive games.[385] Two days later, he recorded his fourth consecutive triple-double of the season with 15 points, 16 rebounds, and 12 assists, in a 120–115 victory against the San Antonio Spurs, breaking his own record for the most consecutive triple-doubles made. He tied the Lakers record for the most consecutive triple-doubles, joining Magic Johnson (1981, 1987) and Russell Westbrook (2021).[386] On December 1, he reached 15,000 career field goals in a 105–104 victory against the Utah Jazz, joining Abdul-Jabbar as the only players to reach said milestone.[387] On December 19 against the Sacramento Kings, he passed Abdul-Jabbar for the most career regular season minutes played.[388]

On January 3, 2025, James put up 30 points and eight assists in a 119–102 win over the Atlanta Hawks. He surpassed Jordan (562) for the most 30-point games in NBA history.[389] On January 21, James posted a triple-double with 21 points, 10 rebounds and 13 assists in a 111–88 win over the Washington Wizards. He became the second NBA player to post a triple-double at age 40 or older, after Karl Malone. On February 1, James registered a triple-double of 33 points, 11 rebounds and 12 assists in a 128–112 win over the New York Knicks. On February 6, James recorded season-highs 42 points and 17 rebounds, along with eight assists, in a 120–112 win over the Golden State Warriors. At 40 years and 38 days, James became the oldest player to score 40+ points. He is also the youngest, at 19 years, 88 days old. He became the first player older than 30 to record 30+ pts, 15+ reb, 5+ ast and 5+ triples in a game.[390] James was selected for his 21st NBA All-Star Game, but missed the 2025 contest due to foot and ankle soreness, ending his streak of consecutive All-Star starts at 20.[391]

On March 4, 2025, James surpassed 50,000 career points across the regular season and playoffs during a 136–115 win against the New Orleans Pelicans.[392] On March 8, James injured his groin in a 111–101 loss to the Boston Celtics, sidelining him.[393] After a seven-game absence, James returned on March 22 in a 146–115 loss to the Chicago Bulls.[394] On March 26, James scored 13 points and a game-winning, buzzer-beating tip-in in a 120–119 victory against the Indiana Pacers.[395] It marked James' eight career game-winning buzzer-beater and his first as a Laker.[396] On April 9, he passed Abdul-Jabbar for second on the league's games played list.[397] On April 27, he logged his 144th career playoff double-double with 27 points and 12 rebounds along with eight assists, three steals and three blocks, in a 116–113 loss to the Minnesota Timberwolves in Game 4 of the first round. He passed Wilt Chamberlain for third in the career playoff double-doubles list.[398] The Lakers lost Game 5 and were eliminated.[399]

On October 9, 2025, the Lakers announced that James would be sidelined for the start of the 2025–26 season due to sciatica on his right side.[400] He missed the Lakers' first game, a 119–109 loss to the Golden State Warriors, marking the first time he missed a season opener.[401] On November 18, James made his season debut with the Lakers in a 140–125 win over the Utah Jazz after missing the first 14 games, becoming the first player to appear in 23 NBA seasons. On December 4, in a 123–120 win over the Toronto Raptors, James assisted on Rui Hachimura's game-winning, buzzer-beating 3-pointer, but finished the game with eight points on 4-of-17 shooting.[402][403] This ended his streak of 1,297 consecutive games with at least 10 points, setting a record. The last time he had scored fewer than 10 points was in January 2007.[404] On January 13, he recorded 31 points, nine rebounds, and 10 assists, just one rebound shy of becoming the oldest player to record a triple-double, in a 141–116 win over the Atlanta Hawks. He passed Bryant to become the player with the most double-doubles with 30+ points in Lakers franchise history.[405]

As a 19-year-old rookie, James made his debut for the United States national team at the 2004 Olympics in Athens, Greece.[406] He spent the Games mostly on the bench,[407] averaging 14.6 minutes per game with 5.8 points, and 2.6 rebounds per game in eight games.[406] Team USA finished the competition with a bronze medal, becoming the first U.S. basketball team to return home without a gold medal since adding active NBA players to their lineup.[408] James felt that his limited playing time was a "lowlight" and believed he was not given "a fair opportunity to play".[407]

At the 2006 FIBA World Championship in Japan, James took on a greater role for Team USA, averaging 13.9 points, 4.8 rebounds, and 4.1 assists per game as co-captain.[409][410] The team finished the tournament with an 8–1 record, winning another bronze medal.[409] James' behavior was again questioned, this time by teammate Bruce Bowen, who confronted James during tryouts regarding his treatment of staff members.[411][412]

Before naming James to the 2008 Olympic team, Team USA managing director Jerry Colangelo and coach Mike Krzyzewski gave James an ultimatum to improve his attitude, and he heeded their advice.[411][413] At the FIBA Americas Championship 2007, he averaged 18.1 points, 3.6 rebounds, and 4.7 assists per game, including a 31-point performance against Argentina in the championship game, the most ever by an American in an Olympic qualifier.[414] Team USA went 10–0, winning the gold medal and qualifying for the 2008 Olympics in Beijing, China.[406] James credited the team's attitude and experience for their improvement, saying: "I don't think we understood what it meant to put on a USA uniform and all the people that we were representing in 2004. We definitely know that now."[415] At the Olympics, Team USA went unbeaten, winning their first gold medal since 2000.[416] In the final game, James' statistics were – 14 points, six rebounds, and three assists against Spain.[417]

James did not play at the 2010 FIBA World Championship but rejoined Team USA for the 2012 Olympics in London, England.[418] He became the leader of the team, with Bryant, who would soon be 34, stepping back.[419] James facilitated the offense from the post and perimeter, called the defensive sets, and provided scoring when needed.[420] During a game against Australia, he recorded the first triple-double in U.S. Olympic basketball history with 11 points, 14 rebounds, and 12 assists.[l] Team USA won their second straight gold medal, again defeating Spain in the final game.[422] James contributed 19 points in the victory, becoming the all-time leading scorer in U.S. men's basketball history.[406][422] He also joined Michael Jordan as the only players to win an NBA MVP award, NBA championship, NBA Finals MVP, and Olympic gold medal in the same year.[423] Afterwards, Krzyzewski said: "[James] is the best player, he is the best leader and he is as smart as anybody playing the game right now."[424]

After a 12-year gap, James rejoined the national team on the 2024 Olympic squad in Paris as Team Captain at 39 years old.[425] Voted by the entire 592-strong U.S. delegation, James was named as one of the two Team USA flag-bearers for the opening ceremony of the games, becoming the first male basketball player to be so honored.[426][427] James led the team in rebounds and assists. He recorded his second Olympic triple double in a comeback win in the semi-final against Serbia with 16 points, 12 rebounds and 10 assists.[428] James became the first player in Olympic history with two triple doubles.[429] Team USA won their fifth straight gold medal, defeating France 98–87 in the final game,[430] with James recording 14 points, 6 rebounds and 10 assists. At the conclusion of the tournament with averages of 14.2 points, 6.8 rebounds and 8.5 assists, James was named the FIBA Men's Olympics MVP and was selected to the FIBA Men's Olympics All-Star Five.[431] James became the third male basketball player to win three gold medals at the Olympics.

Standing 6 feet 9 inches (2.06 m) tall and weighing 250 pounds (113 kg),[432] James has played the majority of his career at the small forward and power forward positions,[83] but he has also been deployed at the other positions when necessary.[433] His playing style, which is athletic and versatile,[137] has drawn comparisons to Basketball Hall of Fame players Oscar Robertson; Magic Johnson and Michael Jordan.[434][435][436] Through the 2024–25 season, James' career averages are 27.0 points, 7.5 rebounds, 7.4 assists, 1.5 steals, and 0.7 blocks per game.[83] Throughout the 2010s, he was usually ranked as the best player in the NBA each season by ESPN and Sports Illustrated.[437][438]

As an 18-year-old rookie, James led the Cavaliers in scoring.[440] He holds numerous "youngest to" distinctions,[441][442] including being the youngest player to score 30,000 career points.[443] During his first stint in Cleveland, James was primarily used as an on-ball point forward, and although his shooting tendencies were perimeter-oriented,[137] he established himself as one of the best slashers and finishers in basketball.[444][445] His combination of speed, quickness, and size often created matchup problems for opposing teams because James was capable of blowing by larger defenders and overpowering smaller ones.[446] These qualities became more apparent in transition, where he developed a reputation for grabbing defensive rebounds and then beating the defense downcourt for highlight reel baskets.[447] Around this time, James was frequently criticized for not having a reliable jump shot or post game.[448] Teams would try to exploit these weaknesses by giving him space in the half court and forcing him to settle for three-pointers and long two-pointers, a strategy famously used by Spurs coach Gregg Popovich in the 2007 Finals, where James converted on only 36 percent of his field goals in four games.[449]

In Miami, Heat coach Erik Spoelstra changed James' role to a more unconventional one.[137] James spent more time in the post and improved his shot selection and accuracy on jump shots.[137][450] He also learned how to work as an off-ball cutter in the Heat's "pass-happy" offense.[451] Behind these improvements, James' overall scoring efficiency rose to historically great levels.[452] During this time, ESPN's Tom Haberstroh called James' free-throw shooting his biggest weakness, describing it as "average".[453] Upon returning to the Cavaliers, James began to experience subtle age-related declines in productivity,[454] posting his lowest scoring averages since his rookie season in 2015 and 2016.[83][455] His shooting also temporarily regressed, and James briefly ranked as the NBA's worst high-volume shooter from outside the paint.[456] Despite these changes, he remained an elite offensive player who beat defenses with body control, strength, and varying attacking speeds.[446]

For most of his career, James has controlled the offense as the primary ball handler on his team.[457] His playmaking ability is generally considered one of his premier skills, and some analysts rank him among the greatest passers in NBA history.[458] By exploiting his size, vision, and the attention James garners from opposing defenses,[459] he creates easy points for his teammates with accurate assists.[460] James executes unconventional passes, including after leaving his feet and through defensive traffic.[461] His uncanny tendency to find the open man has helped force NBA teams to incorporate some elements of zone into their schemes to better cover the weak side of the court and prevent James from passing to open shooters.[446] Early in his career, James was criticized for overpassing in pressure situations, in particular for passing instead of shooting in the waning seconds of close games;[462][463] however, as his career progressed, James' clutch performance was viewed more favorably.[464]

At the beginning of his NBA career, James was considered a poor defensive player,[465] but he improved steadily through the years. In 2009, James became proficient at the chase-down block, which involves coming in from behind the opposition in transition to block the shot.[73] In Miami, he developed into a more versatile defensive player, and the Heat relied on him to guard all five positions.[466] From the years 2012–2016, he was ranked among the top three defenders in the NBA by general managers, earning the vote as the best perimeter defender in the league preceding the 2014–15 NBA season.[467] Along with Shane Battier and Dwyane Wade, Miami used James in an ultra-aggressive defensive scheme,[468] with James cheating off the ball to help out inside or get into rebounding position.[469] Beginning in 2014, some analysts reported a regression in his defensive impact, stemming from a lack of effort and expected age-related declines.[470][471] During his second stint in Cleveland, James' defense progressively declined. After missed drives on offense, he often dawdled back on defense while complaining to the referees; he provided less help off the ball, and was less aggressive in switching.[472] James himself admitted to taking plays off at times, referring to this approach as "chill mode".[473] He eventually developed a reputation for raising his defensive level in the playoffs, which some analysts referred to as "Playoff LeBron".[474]

James left high school as one of the most hyped prospects in NBA history.[m] Upon entering the NBA, he made an immediate impact and was voted Rookie of the Year in his debut season.[480] As of 2024, James has been named to 21 All-NBA Teams, including 13 times to the First Team, which are both NBA records.[274] His four MVP awards are matched only by Michael Jordan, Kareem Abdul-Jabbar, Wilt Chamberlain, and Bill Russell; James and Russell are the only players to win four MVP awards in a five-year span.[481] James has also won four Finals MVP Awards, which is the second-most all-time,[482] and earned All-Defensive honors every season from 2009 to 2014.[83] While James has never won the Defensive Player of the Year Award, he has finished second in the voting twice and lists it as one of his main goals.[72][483] His teams have appeared in the Finals ten times and won four championships; his 10 Finals appearances are tied for third all-time.[n] Some analysts have criticized him for not having a better Finals record, while others have countered that James usually performed well but his team was defeated by superior competition.[485][486][487]

On the basis of his career longevity and on-court performances, sports publications have consistently included James in rankings of the best basketball players in history,[o] and he was named the Associated Press Male Athlete of the Decade for the 2010s.[495] This has resulted in frequent comparisons to Jordan in debates over the sport's all-time best.[p] In a 2016 interview with Sports Illustrated, James acknowledged that his motivation was surpassing Jordan as the greatest.[496] In February 2018, The Ringer spent an entire week devoted to both players, with Bill Simmons ultimately concluding that Jordan was still ahead.[497] In polls, James has ranked second behind Jordan.[498][499][500] The results strongly correlate with age, with older voters more commonly choosing Jordan.[499][500] Davis et al. of Business Insider stated: "The data would suggest that younger, more-engaged NBA fans lean toward James, as he's still playing. Older generations who watched Jordan play and tune in less today lean toward Jordan."[500] Referring to James as the best challenger to Jordan's status as the greatest basketball player of all time, Sam Quinn of CBS Sports stated that "the margin for error where Jordan is involved is overwhelmingly slim" and that "in the rings-obsessed basketball discourse", Jordan having more titles and an "unblemished Finals record holds significant weight".[496]

Fans perceived as overenthusiastic about James have been satirically referred to as Bronsexuals, characterized as having a man crush on Lebron James.[501][502] Furthermore, it is emphasized that amongst that fandom demographic, a bandwagon effect and biases towards Lebron James have obscured clarity in the legacy debate versus Jordan,[503][504][505] such as recency bias.[506]

In addition to praising James' on-court accomplishments, analysts have also noted his influence on player empowerment throughout the NBA, which stemmed from his willingness to change teams during free agency. Ben Golliver of The Washington Post opined that James' move to the Heat in 2010 "defined a decade of player movement", and that he "fundamentally flipped the power balance between stars and their organizations."[507] James' fellow players have also remarked on his influence, such as Warriors forward Draymond Green, who reflected: "We've taken control of our destiny. And I think a lot of people hate that ... I think the doors that he's opened for athletes and especially basketball players is his biggest accomplishment."[508] Multiple current and former NBA players have suggested James' free agency decisions catalyzed the league-wide trend in "superteams" in the 21st century.[509][510][511][512][513]

In 2022, James voiced his desire to play into his forties, potentially alongside or against his sons Bronny and Bryce.[514] This eventually happened when Bronny was selected by the Lakers 55th overall in the 2024 NBA draft, making them the first father-son duo in NBA history.[515] On October 22, 2024, in the season opener against the Minnesota Timberwolves, they shared the court for the first time.[516]

James married his high school sweetheart, Savannah James (née Brinson; born August 27, 1986), on September 14, 2013, in San Diego, California.[517] They have two sons, Bronny and Bryce, and a daughter Zhuri.[514][518] Bronny was a standout high school basketball player, named as a McDonald's All-American in 2023, 20 years after James' selection.[519] James owns a 30,000 square foot mansion in Akron, Ohio that he custom built in 2003 on his property at a cost of $2.1 million.[520] During his stint with the Heat, James resided in Coconut Grove, where he bought a $9 million three-story mansion overlooking Biscayne Bay.[521] In November 2015, James bought a 9,350 square-foot (870 m2) East Coast-style mansion in Brentwood, Los Angeles, for about $21 million.[522] He purchased another home in Brentwood in December 2017 for $23 million.[523] In September 2020, he purchased a third home in Los Angeles, this one in Beverly Hills for $36.75 million.[524]

James' best friends in the NBA are Carmelo Anthony, Chris Paul, and former Heat teammate Dwyane Wade. The four have been referred to as the "banana boat crew". During an excursion to the Bahamas, James rescued Anthony from the water when Anthony was carried away from the boat by the current. During an Instagram Live session, Anthony later recounted: "He saved my life". When asked about how much danger Anthony was in prior to the rescue, James responded: "I don't really know what to say, to be honest. I'm just happy he's still here, obviously."[525]

In September 2023, ESPN reported that a new set of client names from the Biogenesis scandal had been released; included was Ernest "Randy" Mims, a longtime friend and business manager of James, as well as David Alexander, a well-known trainer of prominent athletes who co-owned a cold-pressed juice and smoothie business with Savannah and also served as her personal trainer. The DEA determined that there "was never any indication that LeBron James did anything wrong."[526][527]

James invests heavily in his health, reportedly spending $1.5 million a year to pay for personal chefs, athletic trainers, and physical therapies for recovery. Kyle Korver has described James' fitness as being on "another level". However, James' routine is not perfectly clean; he drinks wine every night, believing it to be good for his heart,[528] while Tristan Thompson has stated that James eats desserts with every meal.[529] In a March 2025 interview, James denied spending that much on his health, claiming he did not know where that number came from.[530]

In January 2009, doctors at the Cleveland Clinic discovered a growth in the right side of James' jaw. Biopsy results showed that James developed a benign jaw tumor, specifically in his parotid gland,[531] which required a five-hour surgery to remove on June 2 after the end of the Cavaliers' run in the 2009 playoffs.[532]

James is considered by fellow NBA players, media tabloids, and popular culture to be the "face of the NBA", often alongside Warriors superstar Stephen Curry.[533][534] His opinions have yielded significant influence on people who make important league decisions; for example, in 2014, James asked commissioner Adam Silver to increase the duration of the All-Star break, and the request was granted the following season.[535] On February 13, 2015, James was elected the first vice president of the National Basketball Players Association (NBPA).[536]

Throughout his career, James has been ranked by Forbes as one of the world's most influential athletes,[q] and has been listed by Time as one of the 100 most influential people in the world.[539] During his first stint with the Cavaliers, James was adored by local fans, and Sherwin-Williams displayed a giant Nike-produced banner of James on its world headquarters.[540] Despite their affection for James, Cleveland fans and critics were frequently annoyed when he sported a Yankees hat when he attended Cleveland Indians baseball games against the New York Yankees.[541] Following his actions during the 2010 free agency period and The Decision, James was listed as one of the most disliked athletes in the United States.[542] By 2013, his image had mostly recovered and he was reported by ESPN as the most popular player in the NBA for the second time in his career.[543] In 2014, James was named the most popular male athlete in America by the Harris Poll.[544] He has led the league in jersey sales six times.[545]

Memorabilia associated with James is highly sought after; two of James' rookie cards are among the most expensive basketball cards ever sold at auction, and one of those cards also briefly held the record for the most expensive modern-day sports card when it sold for $1.8 million at auction in July 2020.[548] A Mike Trout rookie card broke the record for a modern-day card the following month.[549] All jerseys worn in the 2020 NBA All-Star Game were auctioned by the NBA and NBPA to raise funds for charity; James' jersey sold for $630,000, setting a record for a modern-day sports jersey.[550]

In March 2008, James became the first black man, as well as the third man overall after Richard Gere and George Clooney, to appear on the cover of Vogue, when he posed with Gisele Bündchen.[551] In response, ESPN columnist Jemele Hill considered the cover offensive and "memorable for the wrong reasons", describing the demeanor of James and his holding Bündchen as a reference to classic imagery of the movie monster King Kong, a dark savage capturing his fair-skinned love interest.[546][547]

In 2025, Mattel announced that it was adding James to the Barbie roster, "making him the first professional male athlete to be honoured as a Ken doll." According to the BBC, it is "an inch taller than the standard Ken doll."[552] James was announced to be honorary co-chair of the 2025 Met Gala in Manhattan,[553] though he had to skip due to the knee injury he sustained in game 5 of the first round against the Minnesota Timberwolves.[554][555]

James has maintained close ties to his hometown of Akron, Ohio, which is also where his charity foundation, the LeBron James Family Foundation (LJFF), is based.[556] Since 2005, the foundation has held an annual bike-a-thon to raise money for various causes.[557] In 2015, James announced a partnership with the University of Akron to provide scholarships for as many as 2,300 children beginning in 2021.[558] In 2017, he received the J. Walter Kennedy Citizenship Award from the NBA for his "outstanding service and dedication to the community."[559]

In November 2017, the Akron School Board approved the I Promise School, a public elementary school created in a partnership with the LJFF to help struggling elementary school students stay in school.[560] The school officially opened on July 30, 2018, with James reflecting that it was his most important professional accomplishment.[561] Other noteworthy public and charitable initiatives undertaken by James in Akron include the I Promise Institute at the University of Akron,[562] I Promise Village (housing complex),[563] House Three-Thirty (community center/retail plaza),[564] and I Promise Health Quarters (medical center).[10]

James is also an active supporter of various non-profit organizations, including After-School All-Stars, Boys & Girls Clubs of America, and Children's Defense Fund.[565][566][567] In 2016, he donated $2.5 million to the Smithsonian National Museum of African American History and Culture to support an exhibit on Muhammad Ali.[568]

Throughout his career, James has taken public stances on controversial issues, and has mentioned a feeling of obligation to effect change using his status.[569] Those include the War in Darfur,[570] the killing of Trayvon Martin,[571] the now-former NBA owner Donald Sterling's racist comments in 2014,[569] the Michael Brown verdict,[572] the death of Eric Garner,[573] the U.S. national anthem kneeling protests,[574] the shooting of Breonna Taylor,[575] the death of Ma'Khia Bryant,[576] Kyle Rittenhouse,[577] and the ruling of Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health Organization that overturned Roe v. Wade in 2022.[578]

On August 27, 2020, James and his Lakers teammates, as well as the Bucks, began boycotting the 2020 NBA playoffs to protest the shooting of Jacob Blake.[579] In response, senior White House advisor Jared Kushner stated that he was planning to reach out to James regarding the boycott. Following a players' committee to discuss the boycott, James and others reached out to former president Barack Obama, who reportedly advised them to continue playing and finish that year's NBA season.[580]

During the 2019–2020 Hong Kong protests, a statement James made about a since-deleted tweet by Daryl Morey,[581] in which Morey expressed support for the pro-democracy movement in Hong Kong, became the subject of controversy. James said Morey was "misinformed".[582] His statement drew backlash from protesters in the movement, with many taking to social media to use racist language against him.[583][584][585] In February 2022, political commentator Bill Maher called James hypocritical for not taking a critical stance towards the Chinese government's human rights abuses.[586] James had taken various other stands on issues regarding sports, such as the Kaepernick controversy and the Houston Astros sign stealing scandal.[587][588]

In October 2023, in response to the October 7th attacks, James voiced his support for Israel on Instagram.[589] His statement drew backlash for its omission of the Palestinians affected by the crisis the attacks provoked, including from Palestinian-American leader and activist Omar Suleiman.[590][591][592]

"Michelle's brother, who was an excellent basketball player, always says that you can learn a lot about somebody's character by the way they play basketball. And when you see LeBron James, it is not just his power and his speed and his vertical. It is his unselfishness, it is his work ethic, it is his insistence on always making the right play, it is his determination—all of which makes him one of the great players of all time. And you saw it in those last three games, put up some of the most staggering statistics in Finals history. He did it the year before despite injuries, dragging his team along to make a very competitive series. You saw it when this kid from Akron broke down and fell to his knees when he realized that he had finally fulfilled a promise that he had made all those years ago and delivered that championship back to Northeast Ohio."

In June 2008, James donated $20,000 to a committee in support of Barack Obama for the 2008 U.S. presidential election.[594] Later that year, James gathered almost 20,000 people at the then-called Quicken Loans Arena for a viewing of Obama's 30-minute American Stories, American Solutions television advertisement.[595] The advertisement was shown on a large screen above the stage, where Jay-Z later held a free concert.[595] In November 2016, James endorsed and campaigned for Hillary Clinton for the 2016 U.S. presidential election.[596]

Following a racist incident at his Los Angeles home in 2017, James expressed that "being black in America is tough. We got a long way to go for us as a society and for us as African Americans until we feel equal in America."[597] Later on that year, in the aftermath of the Unite the Right rally, James questioned the "Make America Great Again" slogan and said: "It's sad what's going on in Charlottesville. Is this the direction our country is heading? Make America Great Again huh? Our youth deserve better!!"[598] James also called President Donald Trump a "bum" after the president rescinded a White House invitation to Stephen Curry.[599] During a 2018 interview with CNN journalist Don Lemon, James then accused Trump of attempting to divide the country with sports, suggesting that "sports has never been something that divides people it's always been something that brings someone together." He declared that he would "never sit across from him. I'd sit across from Obama though."[600][601] In response, Trump tweeted: "LeBron James was just interviewed by the dumbest man on television, Don Lemon. He made LeBron look smart, which isn't easy to do."[602]

On August 19, 2020, James announced his intentions to support the Joe Biden 2020 presidential campaign and that of his running-mate Kamala Harris in advance of the 2020 U.S. presidential election.[603] James spoke in support of the More Than a Vote movement and encouraged members of the African-American community to vote,[604] saying, "People in our community have been just lied to for so many years. We have people that have had convictions in the past, that've been told they cannot vote because they got a conviction. That is voter suppression."[605]

On October 31, 2024, James announced his support for the Kamala Harris 2024 presidential campaign in the 2024 U.S. presidential election in a video posted on social media.[606]

According to Forbes, in May 2023, James became the first active NBA player to become a billionaire,[607] making him one of the richest celebrities.

James' biography LeBron was published on April 11, 2023, by Jeff Benedict. The biography is based on three years of research and more than 250 interviews.[608]

James has signed numerous endorsement contracts; some of the companies that he has done business with are AT&T,[609] Audemars Piguet,[610] Beats by Dre,[611] Blaze Pizza,[612] Coca-Cola,[613] Dunkin' Brands,[614] Intel,[615] Kia,[616] McDonald's,[617] Nike,[613] PepsiCo,[618] State Farm,[619] and Taco Bell.[620] Coming out of high school, James was the target of a three-way bidding war among Nike, Reebok, and Adidas,[621] eventually signing a seven-year deal with Nike in May 2003[622][623] for approximately $90 million.[624] His signature shoes have performed well for Nike.[625] In 2011, Fenway Sports Group became the sole global marketer of his rights, and as part of the deal, James was granted a minority stake in the English Premier League football club Liverpool,[626] who he has claimed his support for.[627] As a result of his endorsement money and NBA salary, James has been listed as one of the world's highest-paid athletes.[628] In 2013, he surpassed Bryant as the highest paid basketball player in the world, with earnings of $56.5 million.[629] In 2014, James realized a profit of more than $30 million as part of Apple's acquisition of Beats Electronics; he had originally struck a deal to get a small stake in the company at its inception in exchange for promoting its headphones.[630] In 2015, James was ranked the sixth highest earning sportsperson,[631] and third highest in 2016 (after Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi).[632] James has stated that he would like to own an NBA team in the future, albeit in a hands-off capacity.[633] In 2011, James co-founded the designer retail store UNKNWN in Miami, Florida.[634]

During Super Bowl LVI in 2022, James appeared in a Crypto.com advertisement, where he conversed with a CGI version of his younger self, offering advice about the future. The commercial, produced by James' SpringHill Company and directed by Calmatic, did not directly promote the service, sparked social media buzz, and inspired a series of memes centered on the advice he could have offered.[635]

Subsequently, Crypto.com launched an NFT airdrop campaign, distributing 5,550 tokens featuring the NBA champion. Participants were chosen randomly from those who scanned a QR code in the Super Bowl ad.[636] Also, in 2022, James' charity LeBron James Family Foundation, partnered with Crypto.com to educate underserved Akron communities with blockchain-related knowledge and Web3 tools, aiming to ensure inclusive advancement in the digital age.[637]

James and comedian Jimmy Kimmel co-hosted the 2007 ESPY Awards.[638] In other comedic pursuits, he hosted the 33rd-season premiere of Saturday Night Live.[639] James has also tried his hand at acting, appearing in a cameo role on the HBO series Entourage.[640] In 2015, he played himself in the Judd Apatow film Trainwreck,[641] receiving positive reviews for his performance.[642] That same year, James' digital video company Uninterrupted raised $15.8 million from Warner Bros. Entertainment and Turner Sports to help expand the company's efforts to bring athlete-created content to fans. It is hosted on Bleacher Report and is used by several other athletes including Tampa Bay Buccaneers tight end Rob Gronkowski and cornerback Richard Sherman.[643]

James and his business partner Maverick Carter own production company SpringHill Entertainment,[644] whose first work was the Lions Gate documentary More Than a Game, which was released in 2009 and chronicled James' high school years.[645] Series produced by SpringHill include the NBC game show The Wall,[646] the Disney XD sports documentary show Becoming,[647] the Starz sitcom Survivor's Remorse,[648] and the animated web series The LeBrons.[649] In 2016, CNBC aired an unscripted series hosted by James called Cleveland Hustles, where four up-and-coming Northern Ohio entrepreneurs will be financed on the condition of revitalizing a neighborhood in Cleveland.[650] In the 2017 Toronto International Film Festival, a 60-minute Vince Carter documentary entitled The Carter Effect was executive produced by James and Maverick Carter along with rapper Drake and Future the Prince.[651][652] In February 2018, it was announced that James' production company will produce a new film in the House Party series with James expected to make a cameo.[653] Later that month, Fox News host Laura Ingraham told James to "shut up and dribble" as a response to his political agendas.[654] This largely contributed to James creating a documentary film series looking at the changing role of athletes in the current political and cultural climate, aptly named, Shut Up and Dribble on Showtime.[655] James partnered with Arnold Schwarzenegger in 2018 to found Ladder, a company that developed nutritional supplements to help athletes with severe cramps after dealing with that issue during the 2014 Finals.[656]

In February 2019, it was revealed that James would executive produce rapper 2 Chainz's new album Rap or Go to the League.[657] A Def Jam press release said the intent of the album is "celebrating black excellence and focusing on the power of education and entrepreneurship."
